## rangeDecoder  durable/src/env/decode.ts
used by: durable-effect
/**
 * Decoding that matches `new TextDecoder().decode(bytes)` of the whole input when the input arrives in pieces. Node's
 * streaming decoder with BOM handling can drop a U+FEFF that follows a chunk boundary, not only a leading byte-order
 * mark, so these decoders turn BOM handling off and drop a leading mark themselves.
 */

/** A streaming decoder for a byte range; callers that start at the beginning of a file skip a leading mark themselves. */
export function rangeDecoder(): InstanceType<typeof TextDecoder>

## BinaryReader  durable/src/env/index.ts
used by: durable-effect; env-effect via RemoteExecutionEnv
/** Positional reads from one opened regular file; all calls see the same file even if its path is renamed. */
export interface BinaryReader {
	/** Metadata of the opened file, not of whatever its path names now. */
	info(context: Context): Promise<Result<FileInfo, FileError>>;
	/** Up to `length` bytes at `offset`; fewer only at end of file. */
	read(offset: number, length: number, context: Context): Promise<Result<Uint8Array, FileError>>;
	/**
	 * One pass over the file that locates lines `[startLine, endLine)` (`endLine` absent: to the end), 0-based, where line
	 * `k` starts after the `k`-th newline byte. Decoded sizes are those of the text `new TextDecoder().decode(file)` would
	 * produce for that range, so a byte-order mark at the start of the file is not counted.
	 */
	scanLines(options: { startLine: number; endLine?: number }, context: Context): Promise<Result<LineScan, FileError>>;
	close(context: Context): Promise<void>;
}

## DirReader  durable/src/env/index.ts
used by: durable-effect; env-effect via RemoteExecutionEnv
/** Pages of one directory's entries. */
export interface DirReader {
	/**
	 * Up to `maxEntries` entries in the order the file system returns them, continuing where the previous call stopped.
	 * `done` marks the end; it may come with the last entries or with an empty page. An entry that disappears before its
	 * metadata is read is skipped, as are entries of unsupported kinds. After a failed or aborted call, close the reader.
	 */
	next(maxEntries: number, context: Context): Promise<Result<{ entries: FileInfo[]; done: boolean }, FileError>>;
	close(context: Context): Promise<void>;
}

## FileChange  durable/src/env/index.ts
used by: durable-effect; env-effect via RemoteExecutionEnv
/**
 * What changed, tagged by `kind`:
 * - `paths`: something at or below each path may have changed (a directory path covers its whole subtree). Calls may be
 *   spurious; a change is never missed while the watcher is healthy.
 * - `overflow`: coverage was uncertain for a while (lost events, reconnect); rescan everything that is watched.
 * - `failed`: the watcher stopped with `error`, for example because the watched tree grew past the environment's limit;
 *   no calls follow.
 */
export type FileChange =
	| { readonly kind: "paths"; readonly paths: string[] }
	| { readonly kind: "overflow" }
	| { readonly kind: "failed"; readonly error: FileError };

## FileSystem  durable/src/env/index.ts
used by: durable-effect; env-effect via LocalExecutionEnv
/** Portable filesystem capability. Operations return failures rather than throwing. */
export interface FileSystem {
	/**
	 * The file namespace: equal ids see the same files at the same paths, whatever their `cwd`. Every local Node
	 * environment shares one id; each container or remote host has its own.
	 */
	readonly id: string;
	cwd: string;
	absolutePath(path: string, context: Context): Promise<Result<string, FileError>>;
	joinPath(parts: string[], context: Context): Promise<Result<string, FileError>>;
	readTextFile(path: string, context: Context): Promise<Result<string, FileError>>;
	openTextLineReader(path: string, context: Context): Promise<Result<TextLineReader, FileError>>;
	readTextLines(
		path: string,
		options: { maxLines?: number } | undefined,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Result<string[], FileError>>;
	readBinaryFile(path: string, context: Context): Promise<Result<Uint8Array, FileError>>;
	/**
	 * Open a regular file for bounded positional reads. A directory fails with `is_directory`, other non-regular files
	 * with `invalid`. With `noFollow`, a symbolic link as the final path component fails with `invalid` instead of being
	 * followed; earlier components are still resolved.
	 */
	openBinaryReader(
		path: string,
		options: { noFollow?: boolean } | undefined,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Result<BinaryReader, FileError>>;
	writeFile(path: string, content: string | Uint8Array, context: Context): Promise<Result<void, FileError>>;
	appendFile(path: string, content: string | Uint8Array, context: Context): Promise<Result<void, FileError>>;
	/** Truncate or extend a file to exactly `size` bytes. */
	truncateFile(path: string, size: number, context: Context): Promise<Result<void, FileError>>;
	/** Flush file contents and metadata needed to retrieve them from an open file handle. */
	flushFile(path: string, context: Context): Promise<Result<void, FileError>>;
	renameFile(sourcePath: string, destinationPath: string, context: Context): Promise<Result<void, FileError>>;
	fileInfo(path: string, context: Context): Promise<Result<FileInfo, FileError>>;
	listDir(path: string, context: Context): Promise<Result<FileInfo[], FileError>>;
	/**
	 * Optional: the files, directories and symbolic links below a directory, at any depth, for indexes such as file
	 * completion. Symbolic links are not followed; other kinds of files are not listed; entries that cannot be read are
	 * skipped. See `ListFilesOptions` for hidden and ignored files and for the bounds. Fails with `not_supported` when
	 * the environment cannot list right now (an older remote daemon), so callers fall back to their own walk.
	 */
	listFiles?(
		path: string,
		options: ListFilesOptions | undefined,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Result<FileListing, FileError>>;
	openDirReader(path: string, context: Context): Promise<Result<DirReader, FileError>>;
	/**
	 * Report changes to files and directories, for hosts that load resources from the environment. When the returned
	 * watcher exists, coverage is established: a host that watches before it loads cannot miss a change made during the
	 * load. See `FileChange` for what is reported and `FileWatcher.mode` for how reliably.
	 */
	watch(
		targets: readonly WatchTarget[],
		onChange: (change: FileChange) => void,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Result<FileWatcher, FileError>>;
	canonicalPath(path: string, context: Context): Promise<Result<string, FileError>>;
	exists(path: string, context: Context): Promise<Result<boolean, FileError>>;
	createDir(
		path: string,
		options: { recursive?: boolean } | undefined,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Result<void, FileError>>;
	remove(
		path: string,
		options: { recursive?: boolean; force?: boolean } | undefined,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Result<void, FileError>>;
	createTempDir(prefix: string | undefined, context: Context): Promise<Result<string, FileError>>;
	createTempFile(
		options: { prefix?: string; suffix?: string } | undefined,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Result<string, FileError>>;
	cleanup(context: Context): Promise<void>;
}

## FileWatcher  durable/src/env/index.ts
used by: durable-effect; env-effect via RemoteExecutionEnv
export interface FileWatcher {
	/**
	 * `native`: changes are reported within about two seconds. `polling`: the environment compares snapshots, because
	 * the file system does not report changes reliably (network and FUSE file systems); a change undone between two
	 * snapshots can be missed.
	 */
	readonly mode: "native" | "polling";
	/** Stop watching; no `onChange` call starts after this resolves. Idempotent. */
	stop(context: Context): Promise<void>;
}

## LineScan  durable/src/env/index.ts
used by: durable-effect; env-effect via RemoteExecutionEnv
/** Where lines of a file are, as `BinaryReader.scanLines` found them. */
export interface LineScan {
	/** Newline bytes in the whole file; it has `newlines + 1` lines. */
	newlines: number;
	/**
	 * Byte range of the selected lines: from the start of the first to the end of the last, without the newline that
	 * ends it. A selection past the last line is empty at the end of the file.
	 */
	start: number;
	end: number;
	/** Where the first selected line ends: its newline, or the end of the file. */
	firstLineEnd: number;
	/** Where the last selected line starts. */
	lastLineStart: number;
	/** UTF-8 byte length of the decoded selection and of its first line. */
	selectedBytes: number;
	firstLineBytes: number;
}

## ListFilesOptions  durable/src/env/index.ts
used by: durable-effect; env-effect via LocalExecutionEnv
/** What `FileSystem.listFiles` lists. */
export interface ListFilesOptions {
	/**
	 * Include names starting with `.` (on Windows also files with the hidden attribute); default true. Entries named
	 * `.git` are never listed.
	 */
	hidden?: boolean;
	/**
	 * Inside a git work tree, skip what git ignores: the `.gitignore` files of the directory, its subdirectories and its
	 * parents, `.git/info/exclude`, and the global excludes file; default true. Unlike `git ls-files`, a tracked file that
	 * matches an ignore rule is skipped too. Outside work trees, `.gitignore` files have no effect.
	 */
	gitignore?: boolean;
	/** Names of entries to skip with everything below them, such as `node_modules`. */
	exclude?: readonly string[];
	/** Most entries to list; default 50 000. */
	maxEntries?: number;
	/** Most bytes of the listing: each entry's UTF-8 path plus two; default 4 MiB, at most 15.9 MiB. */
	maxBytes?: number;
	/** Time after which the listing stops; default 10 000 ms. */
	timeoutMs?: number;
}

export type Result<TValue, TError> = { ok: true; value: TValue } | { ok: false; error: TError };

## Shell  durable/src/env/index.ts
used by: durable-effect; env-effect via LocalExecutionEnv
export interface Shell {
	/**
	 * Run a command. A string runs through the environment's shell. An array runs `command[0]` directly with the rest
	 * as its arguments, without a shell, so they reach the program unparsed. Aborting the context or a timeout kills
	 * only this command's processes.
	 */
	exec(
		command: string | readonly string[],
		options: ShellExecOptions | undefined,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Result<ShellExecResult, ExecutionError>>;
	/** Kill every command this environment still runs; for its owner's shutdown, never for one request. */
	cleanup(context: Context): Promise<void>;
}

## ShellExecOptions  durable/src/env/index.ts
used by: durable-effect; env-effect via RemoteExecutionEnv
export interface ShellExecOptions {
	cwd?: string;
	env?: Record<string, string>;
	inheritEnv?: boolean;
	timeout?: number;
	/**
	 * Every decoded chunk of stdout and stderr as it arrives, in arrival order, with the stream it came from: raw,
	 * unbounded, and unthrottled. Each stream is decoded separately, so a character split across chunks survives.
	 */
	onOutput?: (text: string, context: Context, info: ShellOutputInfo) => void;
	spill?: ShellSpillOptions;
	/**
	 * The caller keeps only this tail of the output, so the environment may omit output outside it and report the omission
	 * as `info.skipped`. Without it, every chunk is delivered.
	 */
	window?: ShellOutputWindow;
}

## ShellExecResult  durable/src/env/index.ts
used by: durable-effect; env-effect via RemoteExecutionEnv
export interface ShellExecResult {
	exitCode: number;
	/** Temporary file holding the complete raw output, when the spill thresholds were exceeded. */
	spillPath?: string;
}

## ShellOutputInfo  durable/src/env/index.ts
used by: durable-effect; env-effect via RemoteExecutionEnv
export interface ShellOutputInfo {
	stream: "stdout" | "stderr";
	/**
	 * Output omitted immediately before this chunk, only with `window`. The chunk then holds all output after the
	 * omission up to its end, and that is more than the window by at least one byte or one line: more than
	 * `window.maxBytes` bytes or more than `window.maxLines` newlines. So the omitted text can never be in the kept tail.
	 * The omission and such a chunk may span both streams in arrival order; `stream` then names the chunk's last stream.
	 * Callers that need the streams apart do not pass `window`.
	 */
	skipped?: ShellOutputSkip;
}

## ShellOutputSkip  durable/src/env/index.ts
used by: durable-effect; env-effect via RemoteExecutionEnv
/**
 * Output an environment omitted, measured on the decoded text `onOutput` would have received: every U+FFFD counts as
 * three bytes, and no sanitizing is applied.
 */
/** The shape of `OutputSkip` from `@earendil-works/chord/output`, which `OutputBuffer.push()` accepts. */
export interface ShellOutputSkip {
	/** UTF-8 byte length of the omitted text. */
	bytes: number;
	/** Newlines (U+000A) in the omitted text. */
	newlines: number;
	/** Whether the omitted text ends with a newline. */
	endsWithNewline: boolean;
}

## ShellOutputWindow  durable/src/env/index.ts
used by: durable-effect; env-effect via RemoteExecutionEnv
/**
 * The tail of the combined output a caller keeps, and how often it samples it. An environment that transfers output
 * over a slow link uses it to omit what the caller would drop anyway and to send no faster than the caller commits.
 */
export interface ShellOutputWindow {
	/** UTF-8 bytes of decoded text kept at the end of the output. */
	maxBytes: number;
	/** Lines kept at the end of the output. */
	maxLines: number;
	/** Minimum pause between the caller's samples of the output. */
	minIntervalMs: number;
	/** Each sample also pauses the caller in proportion to its size at this rate. */
	bytesPerSecond: number;
}

## ShellSpillOptions  durable/src/env/index.ts
used by: durable-effect; env-effect via RemoteExecutionEnv
/** Spill the complete output to a temporary file once it exceeds either threshold. */
export interface ShellSpillOptions {
	afterBytes: number;
	/** Complete or partial lines. */
	afterLines: number;
}

## WatchTarget  durable/src/env/index.ts
used by: durable-effect; env-effect via RemoteExecutionEnv
/** A file or directory to watch. It may be missing; creating it is a change. */
export interface WatchTarget {
	path: string;
	/** Watch everything below a directory, not only its entries. Symbolic links below it are not followed. */
	recursive?: boolean;
	/** Entries below `path` that are neither watched nor reported: names starting with `.`, or these names. */
	exclude?: { hidden?: boolean; names?: readonly string[] };
}

## LineScanner  durable/src/env/line-scan.ts
used by: durable-effect
/**
 * Computes a `LineScan` from a file's bytes fed in order, so an environment can scan any size in bounded memory. Decoded
 * sizes use the same streaming WHATWG decoder as decoding the whole file at once.
 */
export class LineScanner {
	/** `startLine` and `endLine` must be non-negative integers with `endLine > startLine`; `endLine` absent: to the end. */
	constructor(startLine: number, endLine = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)
	push(chunk: Uint8Array): void
	finish(): LineScan
}

## NodeWatchOptions  durable/src/env/node-watch.ts
used by: durable-effect; env-effect via LocalExecutionEnv
/** How `NodeExecutionEnv` watches. */
export interface NodeWatchOptions {
	/**
	 * Force a mode. By default `polling` is chosen on Windows, where native watchers keep directories open and so block
	 * renaming their parents, and for file systems that do not report remote changes.
	 */
	mode?: "native" | "polling";
	/** Interval between snapshots in `polling` mode; default 2000 ms. */
	pollIntervalMs?: number;
	/** Most directories one watcher covers; default 10,000. */
	maxDirectories?: number;
}

export class NodeExecutionEnv implements ExecutionEnv {
	/** Every local environment sees the same files. */

	cwd: string
	constructor(options: { cwd: string; shellPath?: string; shellEnv?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv; watch?: NodeWatchOptions })

		path: string,
		options: { recursive?: boolean } | undefined,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Result<void, FileError>>

		path: string,

		context: Context,
	): Promise<Result<void, FileError>>

	): Promise<Result<string, FileError>>

}

## applyChange  durable/src/harness/agent.ts  watched
used by: thread-effect/src/rivet/fork-agent.ts
why: P177: the bound of maxTurns (an integer 1 or more), and which fields of an agent change Pi applies.
function applyChange(state: Draft<AgentState>, change: AgentChange): void {
	const set = <K extends keyof AgentState>(key: K, value: AgentState[K] | null | undefined) => {
		if (value === undefined) return;
		if (value === null) delete state[key];
		else state[key] = value as Draft<AgentState>[K];
	};
	set("model", change.model === undefined || change.model === null ? change.model : { ...change.model });
	set("thinkingLevel", change.thinkingLevel);
	const extensions = change.extensions;
	set(
		"extensions",
		extensions === undefined || extensions === null
			? extensions
			: isList(extensions)
				? names(extensions)
				: {
						...(extensions.add === undefined ? {} : { add: names(extensions.add) }),
						...(extensions.remove === undefined ? {} : { remove: names(extensions.remove) }),
					},
	);
	const tools = change.tools;
	set(
		"tools",
		tools === undefined || tools === null ? tools : isList(tools) ? names(tools) : { remove: names(tools.remove) },
	);
	const modelTools = change.modelTools;
	set(
		"modelTools",
		modelTools === undefined || modelTools === null
			? modelTools
			: isList(modelTools)
				? names(modelTools)
				: {
						...(modelTools.remove === undefined ? {} : { remove: names(modelTools.remove) }),
						...(modelTools.add === undefined ? {} : { add: names(modelTools.add) }),
					},
	);
	set("instructions", change.instructions);
	set("cwd", change.cwd);
	const maxTurns = change.maxTurns;
	if (maxTurns !== undefined && maxTurns !== null && !(Number.isSafeInteger(maxTurns) && maxTurns >= 1)) {
		throw new RangeError(`maxTurns must be an integer 1 or more, got ${String(maxTurns)}`);
	}
	set("maxTurns", maxTurns);
	const compaction = change.compaction;
	set("compaction", compaction === undefined || compaction === null ? compaction : compactionSettings(compaction));
}

## compactionFields  durable/src/harness/agent.ts  watched
used by: thread-effect/src/rivet/fork-agent.ts
why: P177: the bounds of a token count (an integer 0 or more).
/** The set fields of `policy`; throws a `RangeError` for a token count that is not an integer `0` or more. */
function compactionFields(policy: Partial<CompactionPolicy>): Partial<CompactionPolicy> {
	const fields: Partial<CompactionPolicy> = policy.enabled === undefined ? {} : { enabled: policy.enabled };
	for (const key of TOKEN_FIELDS) {
		const value = policy[key];
		if (value === undefined) continue;
		if (!(Number.isSafeInteger(value) && value >= 0)) {
			throw new RangeError(`compaction.${key} must be an integer 0 or more, got ${String(value)}`);
		}
		fields[key] = value;
	}
	return fields;
}

why: P177: the compaction token counts whose bounds the fork wire repeats.

 * Built-in compaction task (spec §8.7): select an old prefix of the model context, summarize it, and place a summary

## createCompaction  durable/src/harness/compaction.ts  watched
used by: durable-rivet-effect/src/protocol.ts
why: P068: an automatic compaction is a background task; the fork protocol assumes it is Pi's only one.
/**
 * Create a compaction task with its status in this commit. `owner` is the generation that waits for it (a blocking
 * compaction); without one it is conversation-owned, and `background` unless it is manual.
 */
export async function createCompaction(
	tx: Tx,
	conversationId: ConversationId,
	input: CompactionInput,
	owner?: TaskId,
): Promise<TaskId<CompactionResult>> {
	const ownership =
		owner === undefined ? ({ kind: "conversation" } as const) : { kind: "task" as const, taskId: owner };
	const background = owner === undefined && input.reason !== "manual";
	const taskId = await tx.createTask(CompactionTask, input, { ownership, conversationId, background });
	const status = { taskId, trigger: input.reason, blocking: owner !== undefined, attempt: 1 };
	addCompactionStatus(await tx.doc(LiveDoc, conversationId), status);
	return taskId;
}

## GenerationCheckpoint  durable/src/harness/generation.ts
used by: durable-effect
export type GenerationCheckpoint =
	| {
			phase: "prepare";
			attempt: number;
			/** The blocking compaction this generation waited for; it starts no other compaction (spec §8.3). */
			compacted?: TaskId<CompactionResult>;
			/** Error text of the overflow that started `compacted`; checked once when `prepare` resumes. */
			overflow?: string;
			/** Set when the blocking threshold started `compacted`; its outcome is checked once when `prepare` resumes. */
			threshold?: true;
	  }
	| {
			phase: "request";
			attempt: number;
			compacted?: TaskId<CompactionResult>;
			model: ModelRef;
			thinkingLevel: ModelThinkingLevel;
			/** The settings' request options when preparation committed; a resend after recovery uses them unchanged. */
			streamOptions: ConversationStreamOptions;
			/** Newest entry included in the request. */
			cutoff: EntryId;
	  }
	| {
			phase: "retry";
			attempt: number;
			compacted?: TaskId<CompactionResult>;
			until: number;
			/**
			 * The deferred response a poll was fetching when the host died: the next attempt polls it again instead of
			 * sending another request, so the provider's job is neither lost nor paid twice. Absent otherwise.
			 */
			poll?: { model: ModelRef; thinkingLevel?: ModelThinkingLevel; cutoff: EntryId; handle: DeferredHandle };
	  }
	| {
			phase: "poll";
			attempt: number;
			compacted?: TaskId<CompactionResult>;
			model: ModelRef;
			/** Absent in checkpoints of earlier versions. */
			thinkingLevel?: ModelThinkingLevel;
			cutoff: EntryId;
			handle: DeferredHandle;
			pollAt: number;
	  }
	| {
			/** Waiting on the round's tool tasks, which the generation owns (spec §8.5). */
			phase: "tools";
			/** The tool-calling answer. */
			assistant: EntryId;
			/** Tool tasks created so far, in call order; grows by one per started call of a sequential round. */
			tools: TaskId<ToolTaskResult>[];
			/** Calls of a sequential round not started yet, in call order. */
			pending: string[];
	  }
	| {
			/**
			 * The run answered: its answer is committed and its inputs settled, and it keeps `pi.live.run` while `afterRun`
			 * hooks are asked for tasks (spec §8.3). A crash here asks them again: nothing was created yet.
			 */
			phase: "finish";
			run: RunSummary;
	  }
	| {
			/** Waiting on the tasks `afterRun` hooks asked for, which the generation owns; then the run ends. */
			phase: "drain";
			answer: EntryId;
			tasks: TaskId[];
	  }
	| {
			/**
			 * The round is complete and waits on the tasks `afterTools` hooks asked for, which the generation owns; then it
			 * ends as the `tools` phase ends it (spec suspendable §6). A crash before they exist asks the hooks again.
			 */
			phase: "afterTools";
			assistant: EntryId;
			tools: TaskId<ToolTaskResult>[];
			tasks: TaskId[];
	  }
	| {
			/**
			 * The answer is appended, and the run's inputs stay open while the tasks an `onYield` hook asked for, which the
			 * generation owns, decide whether it stands (`LiveRun.yield`).
			 */
			phase: "yield";
			answer: EntryId;
			tasks: TaskId[];
	  };

export type CompactionFailure = {

## CompactionStatus  durable/src/harness/live.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Presentation of one live compaction task (spec §8.7). */
export type CompactionStatus = {
	taskId: TaskId<CompactionResult>;
	/** What started it: `compact()`, a threshold, or a context overflow. */
	trigger: CompactionReason;
	/** Whether a generation waits for it: a compaction the generation owns. */

	attempt: number;
	/** Durable backoff before the next summarization attempt. */

};

## LiveRun  durable/src/harness/live.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Run control (spec §8.2). */
export type LiveRun = {
	/** The task that settles the run's inputs: its generation, handed from one to the next. */
	taskId: TaskId;
	/** The run's placed inputs, settled when it ends; `[]` once it answered and runs only its `afterRun` tasks. */
	inputs: SubmissionId[];
	/** Tool rounds so far, which `AgentState.maxTurns` bounds; an `onYield` continuation starts the count over. */
	turns: number;
	/**
	 * The run's first entry: the first one the boundary that started it placed, a continue's the failed run's it
	 * continues; otherwise its first tool-calling answer. A run started before it was recorded may lack it; `afterRun`
	 * hooks then get the answer as the first entry.
	 */
	first?: EntryId;
	/**
	 * Present once the run answered and its generation waits for the tasks `afterRun` hooks asked for, listed once
	 * created: queued items stay queued until they are terminal, and the run then ends without a failure.
	 */
	afterRun?: { tasks?: TaskId[] };
	/**
	 * Present while tasks an `onYield` hook asked for decide whether the answer stands (spec suspendable §6): the
	 * answer's entry, which the tasks read, and the tasks. The inputs stay open; every exit but a continuation settles
	 * them `done` with this answer.
	 */
	yield?: { answer: EntryId; tasks: TaskId[] };
};

## LiveState  durable/src/harness/live.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Built-in live conversation state: run control and presentation of the current generation and tool round. */
export type LiveState = {
	/** Run control; present exactly while busy, also while a run that answered runs its `afterRun` tasks. */
	run?: LiveRun;
	/** Presentation of the current generation attempt. */
	generation?: {
		attempt: number;
		/** Committed throttled partial of the in-flight response. */
		message?: JsonRepresentation<AssistantMessage>;
		/** Durable backoff before the next attempt. */
		retry?: { at: number; error: string };
		/** Provider-side deferred response being polled. */
		deferred?: { pollAt: number };
	};
	/** The current tool round in call order, from the tool-calling answer until the generation's `tools` phase ends it. */
	tools?: ToolSlot[];
	/**
	 * Nested calls of running tool calls, in creation order, so a parent precedes its children and task IDs ascend. A
	 * call's nested slots are removed when the call settles.
	 */
	nestedTools?: NestedToolSlot[];
	/** Live compaction tasks in task ID order; absent when none. */
	compactions?: CompactionStatus[];
	/**
	 * The newest compaction failure, so a client can show it after the task ended. A compaction that produces a summary
	 * removes it; one that is aborted or finds nothing to compact leaves it.
	 */
	compactionFailure?: CompactionFailure;
	/**
	 * Why the newest run ended without an answer, so a client can show it after the run ended. Set in the commit that
	 * ends the run; removed when a later commit starts a run. A run started in the same commit, by
	 * `afterFailedRun: "continue"` or after a reset, keeps it.
	 */
	runFailure?: RunFailure;
};

## NestedToolSlot  durable/src/harness/live.ts
used by: durable-effect
/**
 * Presentation of one nested call: a call a running tool made through `executeTool()`. `callId` is
 * `<parentCallId>/<key>`, the call's ID, unique because keys contain no `/`. The Harness relates
 * slots by task ID: `taskId` is the call's tool task, `parentTaskId` the calling one, model-issued or nested.
 */
export type NestedToolSlot = SlotProgress & {
	parentCallId: string;
	parentTaskId: TaskId;
	taskId: TaskId;
	/**
	 * What the call was made with, replaced by the arguments it runs with, after repair, `beforeTool`, and coercion,
	 * once it starts executing. A model-issued call's arguments are in its assistant entry instead.
	 */
	arguments: JsonObject;
	/** Once done: how the call ended, for a status line. The result itself is in the caller's `NestedCallDoc`. */
	summary?: NestedToolSummary;
};

## NestedToolSummary  durable/src/harness/live.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** How a nested call ended: an error flag, its execution time, its spend, and up to 500 characters of error text. */
export type NestedToolSummary = {
	isError: boolean;
	durationMs?: number;
	usage?: JsonRepresentation<Usage>;
	error?: string;
};

## RunFailure  durable/src/harness/live.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** The newest run that ended without an answer (spec §8.2). */
export type RunFailure = {
	/** The task that ended the run: the run's task at its end. */
	taskId: TaskId;
	/** The run's inputs, settled `unanswered`. */
	inputs: SubmissionId[];
	reason: RunFailureReason;
	/**
	 * `model_error`: the error text; `no_model`: which model is missing; `faulted`: the error message; `orphaned`: why
	 * the task could not run (`missing_task`, `task_too_old`, `migration_failed`); `interrupted` and `restart_limit`: what
	 * was cut off, and how often; `turn_limit`: the tool rounds the run took, `"1 turn"` or `"N turns"`.
	 */
	detail?: string;
	/** The failed run's `run.first`, so a continue's `afterRun` hooks see its history too. */
	first?: EntryId;
};

## RunFailureReason  durable/src/harness/live.ts
used by: durable-effect
/**
 * Why a run ended without an answer:
 * - `model_error`: the model's response failed, after any retries, or the compaction a request needed failed;
 * - `no_model`: no model is configured, or the configured one is not available;
 * - `aborted`: the run was aborted (`Conversation.abort()`, `abortTask()`); `detail` says when its abort handler was
 *   cut off `settings.restartLimit` times and did not finish;
 * - `reset`: a queued reset started a new context at the post-tools boundary, before an answer (a tool's handoff
 *   continues the run);
 * - `faulted`: the run's task threw where it cannot recover, or storage rejected its commit;
 * - `orphaned`: the run's task was aborted while no registered definition could take it;
 * - `interrupted`: the host stopped while the model was answering, more often than `settings.retry` retries;
 * - `restart_limit`: the run's generation was cut off `settings.restartLimit` times in a row; a request or poll it was
 *   cut off during counts as a failed attempt first, so this ends one whose charge itself keeps failing;
 * - `nothing_to_answer`: the context did not end in a user message or tool results (empty, or ending in an answer), so
 *   no request was sent, as for a continue after an answer;
 * - `turn_limit`: a tool round reached the conversation's `maxTurns`; a continue resumes on its results.
 */
export type RunFailureReason =
	| "model_error"
	| "no_model"
	| "aborted"
	| "reset"
	| "faulted"
	| "orphaned"
	| "interrupted"
	| "restart_limit"
	| "nothing_to_answer"
	| "turn_limit";

## TaskScheduler.#inScope  durable/src/harness/scheduler.ts  watched
used by: durable-effect/src/idle.ts
why: P041: Pi's idle rule (walk owners up, a background task stops the walk), restated without waiting.
	/**
	 * Whether ordinary traversal from `scope` reaches `start`: walking up reaches the scope's conversation, or an
	 * ownerless one for `roots`, without crossing a background owner, unless `crossBackground`. `undefined` while an
	 * edge is not loaded.
	 */
	#inScope(start: Up, scope: Scope, crossBackground = false): boolean | undefined {
		this.#record(INTENT_KEY);
		for (const step of this.#above(start)) {
			if (step.kind === "unknown") return undefined;
			if (step.kind === "conversation") {
				if (scope.kind === "conversation" && step.conversation === scope.conversation) return true;
			} else if (step.node.background && !crossBackground) {
				return false;
			}
		}
		return scope.kind === "roots";
	}

## checkInputEntry  durable/src/harness/submissions.ts  watched
used by: recorder-effect/src/from-entry.ts
why: P120: the pi. prefix of the kinds Pi reserves for its own entries.
/** Reject an input entry an untyped caller got wrong: its kind must be a non-empty string outside the `pi.` prefix. */
function checkInputEntry(entry: InputEntry): void {
	const { kind } = entry;
	if (typeof kind !== "string" || kind.length === 0 || kind.startsWith("pi.")) {
		throw new TypeError(
			`An input entry's kind must be a non-empty string not starting with "pi.", got ${String(kind)}`,
		);
	}
}

## NestedCallDoc  durable/src/harness/tool.ts

/**
 * The nested calls of a tool call, a task-scoped family of the calling task keyed by the nested call's key: so a rerun
 * finds the calls it already made, and the caller reads each result. Created with the nested task; the nested call's
 * terminal commit adds its result. One document per call, so no commit rewrites the others. Retires with the caller.

## NestedCallState  durable/src/harness/tool.ts

 * One key of a running tool: a nested call, its task and once it ended its result, or a task created under the key

## ToolTask  durable/src/harness/tool.ts
used by: durable-effect
/**
 * Built-in tool task: resolves the called tool among its phase agent's tools, validates, runs `beforeTool`, records intent,
 * executes, runs `afterTool`, and settles the result, all in one `call` handler so nothing separates resolution from
 * settlement. A call that parks runs again in `parked`, which resolves the tool, records intent, and executes in one
 * handler too. `execute` is reached only by recovery and applies the replay rule. A model-issued call settles by
 * appending its result entry; a nested call by writing its result to its caller's `NestedCallDoc`.
 */
export const ToolTask: Task<ToolTaskInput, ToolTaskCheckpoint, ToolTaskResult, ToolHooks>

## ToolTaskCheckpoint  durable/src/harness/tool.ts

export type ToolTaskCheckpoint =
	| { phase: "call" }
	/**
	 * Durable intent: the final arguments and the replay policy recorded before execution, and for a run after a park,
	 * why it woke and what it parked with. `execute()` runs in the phase that commits it; this phase is reached only by
	 * recovery.
	 */
	| { phase: "execute"; arguments: JsonObject; replay: "safe" | "unsafe"; wake?: WakeReason; checkpoint?: JsonValue }
	/** The call is parked: the `sleeping` or `waiting` state holds this checkpoint (spec suspendable §4.2). */
	| { phase: "parked"; arguments: JsonObject; replay: "safe" | "unsafe"; checkpoint?: JsonValue };

## ConversationTranscript  durable/src/harness/transcript.ts
used by: durable-effect
/**
 * What a client has of one conversation: every entry it got from a view or fetched, and the gaps between (spec §9.3).
 * A layer over any `ConversationView`, wherever it comes from: call `merge()` with every value of the view; it returns
 * the view with the client's whole transcript as `items` instead of the window. Entries never change once committed,
 * so the transcript only grows; a window that dropped its oldest entries keeps them here.
 *
 * A window whose `before` lies past the newest entry the client has does not continue it, after a stall, an overflow,
 * or a reconnect: the entries in between become a gap. Nothing counts entries or computes ranges from entry IDs, which
 * have holes; only exclusive bounds are turned into the inclusive bounds of `EntryQuery`. After a drop, a new watch
 * with `resume` as its window continues the transcript.
 *
 * A merge costs O(items) and never re-sorts or re-fetches; a merge, `loadEarlier()`, or `fillGap()` that adds nothing
 * returns the previous `items` array. Concurrent calls of `loadEarlier()`, or of `fillGap()` for the same gap, share one
 * load, so a placeholder that stays visible does not fetch twice.
 */
export class ConversationTranscript {
	constructor(load: EntryLoader, options?: ConversationTranscriptOptions)
	/**
	 * The ID the transcript reaches: its newest entry, or the `before` of a later window that was empty. Undefined before
	 * the first merge and for an empty transcript.
	 */
	get newest(): EntryId | undefined
	/**
	 * The window that resumes this transcript after a drop: `{ from }` right after `newest`, so a new watch returns only
	 * what was missed when it fits its window, otherwise its newest entries and a gap; `{}` for an empty transcript;
	 * undefined before the first merge. `conversation.watch(context, transcript.resume)`.
	 */
	get resume(): ConversationWindow | undefined
	/** Take one value of the view: its window's entries join the transcript. */
	merge(view: ConversationView): TranscriptView
	/** Load the page before the oldest entry held. Without anything earlier, returns the current view. */
	loadEarlier(context: Context): Promise<TranscriptView>
	/**
	 * Load the next page of `gap`, a gap item of `items`, shrinking it from its start, or removing it once nothing is
	 * missing. A gap that has shrunk since loads the gap it became; one that is no longer there returns the current view.
	 */
	fillGap(gap: Gap, context: Context): Promise<TranscriptView>
}

## ConversationTranscriptOptions  durable/src/harness/transcript.ts
used by: durable-effect
export type ConversationTranscriptOptions = {
	/** Entries `loadEarlier()` and `fillGap()` load per call; default 50. */
	readonly pageSize?: number;
};

## EntryLoader  durable/src/harness/transcript.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Pages a conversation's entries, as `Conversation.entries()` does without a cursor. */
export type EntryLoader = (
	query: Omit<EntryQuery, "conversationId">,
	limit: number,
	context: Context,
) => Promise<Page<EntryRecord, Cursor>>;

## Gap  durable/src/harness/transcript.ts
used by: durable-effect via ConversationTranscript
type Gap = Extract<TranscriptItem, { kind: "gap" }>;

## TranscriptItem  durable/src/harness/transcript.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** One row of a client's transcript. */
export type TranscriptItem =
	| { readonly kind: "entry"; readonly entry: EntryRecord }
	/** Entries strictly between `after` and `upTo` are missing: render "load more" and call `fillGap()`. */
	| { readonly kind: "gap"; readonly after: EntryId; readonly upTo: EntryId }
	/** The transcript continues above: render "load earlier" and call `loadEarlier()`. Always the first item. */
	| { readonly kind: "earlier" };

## TranscriptView  durable/src/harness/transcript.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** The conversation view as a renderer sees it: `items`, the client's whole transcript, instead of the window. */
export type TranscriptView = Omit<ConversationView, "entries" | "before"> & {
	readonly items: readonly TranscriptItem[];
};

## AfterFailedRun  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/**
 * What a failed run does with the inputs queued behind it (`HarnessSettings.afterFailedRun`): a run that ends with
 * `model_error`, `no_model`, `interrupted`, `restart_limit`, `nothing_to_answer`, or `turn_limit`.
 */
export type AfterFailedRun = "keep" | "continue" | "withdraw";

## AfterToolsDecision  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** What an `afterTools` task completes with to end the run after this round. */
export type AfterToolsDecision = { readonly terminate?: true };

## Agent  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** A conversation's agent resolved against a registry snapshot and the settings. */
export type Agent<Tool extends ToolRegistration = ToolRegistration> = {
	readonly model?: ModelRef;
	readonly thinkingLevel: ModelThinkingLevel;
	readonly extensions: readonly Extension<Tool>[];
	/** The tools a request offers, in order: enabled, callable by the model, and selected by `modelTools`. */
	readonly tools: readonly Tool[];
	/** The tools nested calls (`executeTool()`) resolve among, in order: enabled and callable by tools. */
	readonly callable: readonly Tool[];
	/** Enabled deferred tools the model may call and is not offered yet, in registry order: what `tool_search` loads. */
	readonly deferred: readonly Tool[];
	/** Extension sections, then `instructions` when set. */
	readonly sections: readonly PromptSection<Tool>[];
	readonly instructions?: string;
	readonly cwd?: string;
	/**
	 * Tool rounds one run takes at most (`pi.live.run.turns`): the round that reaches it runs its tools, then the run ends
	 * `unanswered` with `turn_limit`. An integer, `1` or more; unset, no limit. Task-owned children and forks inherit it.
	 */
	readonly maxTurns?: number;
	/** This conversation's compaction settings over the harness's (`AgentState.compaction`). */
	readonly compaction?: CompactionSettings;
};

## AgentChange  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** A change to `pi.agent`: a given field replaces the stored one, `null` clears it, `undefined` changes nothing. */
export type AgentChange = {
	readonly model?: ModelRef | null;
	readonly thinkingLevel?: ModelThinkingLevel | null;
	readonly extensions?:
		| readonly Extension[]
		| { readonly add?: readonly Extension[]; readonly remove?: readonly Extension[] }
		| null;
	readonly tools?: readonly ToolRegistration[] | { readonly remove: readonly ToolRegistration[] } | null;
	/** Replaces the stored filter as a whole; tools loaded with `control.addTools` are in its `add`. */
	readonly modelTools?:
		| readonly ToolRegistration[]
		| { readonly remove?: readonly ToolRegistration[]; readonly add?: readonly ToolRegistration[] }
		| null;
	readonly instructions?: string | null;
	readonly cwd?: string | null;
	/** `configure()` throws a `RangeError` unless it is an integer `1` or more (or `null`). */
	readonly maxTurns?: number | null;
	/** Replaces the stored settings as a whole; `configure()` throws a `RangeError` unless every token count is an integer `0` or more. */
	readonly compaction?: CompactionSettings | null;
};

## AgentState  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Stored choices of one conversation; names, not objects. Unset fields follow the host. */
export type AgentState = {
	model?: ModelRef;
	thinkingLevel?: ModelThinkingLevel;
	/** An array selects exactly these extensions, in order. An object edits the host default selection. */
	extensions?: string[] | { add?: string[]; remove?: string[] };
	/** Filters the selected extensions' tools: the enabled tools. An array enables exactly these, in order. */
	tools?: string[] | { remove: string[] };
	/**
	 * Filters the enabled tools the model may call (`callers` includes `model`): the tools offered to it. Never widens:
	 * other tools can still call the ones it leaves out.
	 * - Unset: every such tool except deferred ones.
	 * - An array: exactly these, in order, deferred ones too.
	 * - An object: every such tool except deferred ones and those in `remove`, in registry order, followed by the
	 *   deferred tools in `add` that are not in `remove`, in `add` order. Names of tools that are not deferred or not
	 *   registered have no effect in `add`.
	 */
	modelTools?: string[] | { remove?: string[]; add?: string[] };
	/** Rendered after every extension section, as the section `instructions`. */
	instructions?: string;
	/** Directory within the environment's file system, passed to `HarnessOptions.env`. */
	cwd?: string;
	/**
	 * Tool rounds one run takes at most (`pi.live.run.turns`): the round that reaches it runs its tools, then the run ends
	 * `unanswered` with `turn_limit`. An integer, `1` or more; unset, no limit. Task-owned children and forks inherit it.
	 */
	maxTurns?: number;
	/**
	 * This conversation's compaction settings over the harness's, field by field: its `modelOverrides` entry, then the
	 * harness's, then its own fields, then the harness-wide policy. Its `enabled: false` also beats the harness's model
	 * override. Task-owned children and forks inherit it.
	 */
	compaction?: CompactionSettings;
};

## CompactionHooks  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Hooks of the built-in compaction task. */
export interface CompactionHooks {
	/**
	 * After range selection, before summarizing; the first decision wins. `entries` are the active entries the summary
	 * replaces, the head marker first, and `messages` their model context, the summarizer's source; `firstKept` is the
	 * first entry kept verbatim.
	 */
	beforeCompact(
		compaction: {
			readonly reason: CompactionReason;
			readonly entries: readonly EntryRecord[];
			readonly messages: readonly Message[];
			readonly firstKept: EntryId;
			readonly instructions?: string;
		},
		api: HookApi,
		context: Context,
	): HookResult<{ readonly kind: "decline" } | { readonly kind: "summary"; readonly summary: string }>;
}

## CompactionPolicy  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Automatic compaction thresholds (spec §8.7); manual compaction ignores `enabled`. */
export type CompactionPolicy = {
	/** Threshold and overflow compaction. */
	enabled: boolean;
	/** Room kept free for the answer: generation blocks to compact above `contextWindow - reserveTokens`. */
	reserveTokens: number;
	/** Approximate size of the recent context a summary keeps verbatim. */
	keepRecentTokens: number;
	/** Background compaction starts `backgroundTokens` below the blocking threshold; `0` disables it. */
	backgroundTokens: number;
};

/** Why a compaction runs: `compact()`, a threshold in generation preparation, or a context overflow. */
export type CompactionReason = "manual" | "threshold" | "overflow";

 * `entryId` of a blocking compaction's summary, or the `submissionId` of a conversation-owned compaction's summary
 * write; both absent when nothing was compacted.
 */
export type CompactionResult = { entryId?: EntryId; submissionId?: SubmissionId };

## CompactionSettings  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/**
 * Compaction settings of the harness (`HarnessSettings.compaction`) or of one conversation (`AgentState.compaction`).
 * `modelOverrides` is keyed by exact `"provider/modelId"`; each field it sets replaces the general one for that model,
 * so small- and large-window models can share a harness.

export type CompactionSettings = Partial<CompactionPolicy> & {

## ContextView  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Raw active transcript and derived model context. */
export type ContextView = {
	/** Newest applicable head marker, if any. */
	readonly head: EntryRecord | undefined;
	/** Raw active entries: the head marker followed by non-head entries from its head through the tail. */
	readonly entries: readonly EntryRecord[];

## Conversation  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Stateless handle for one conversation, bound to the Harness that returned it. Compare handles by `id`. */
export interface Conversation {
	readonly id: ConversationId;

	/** Resolved with the current registry snapshot and settings. */
	agent(context: Context): Promise<Agent>;
	/** `configure()` in its own commit. */
	configure(change: AgentChange, context: Context): Promise<void>;

	/**
	 * Durably admit user input, a passive entry write, or a continue. A busy conversation, or one with queued items,
	 * queues input and writes that affect model context in `pi.inbox`; `whenBusy: "reject"` rejects input with
	 * `ConversationBusy` instead and writes nothing. An idle conversation rejects `whenIdle: "reject"` input with
	 * `ConversationIdle` and writes nothing. A write of only `kind` and `data` (no `model`, `head`, or `edits`)
	 * is appended at once, even mid-run, as it changes nothing the model sees. A continue starts a run on the context as
	 * it is, after placing queued items; a busy conversation rejects it with `ConversationBusy`, as it never queues.
	 */
	submit(submission: SubmissionDraft, context: Context): Promise<Submission>;
	/**
	 * Admit a submission inside the caller's commit `tx` (`Harness.commit()`, `Conversation.commit()`, a task's
	 * `runtime.commit()`), with the same rules, and return its ID: the admission is stored with that commit, or not at all
	 * when the callback throws later or the commit fails. Call it before the commit's first table write (`appendEntry()`,
	 * `createTask()`, `createSubmission()`, another admission): otherwise it throws `ReadAfterWrite`, on every path.
	 * Documents may be read and written before and after it. A rejection (`ConversationBusy`, `ConversationIdle`) throws
	 * before any write, so the callback may catch it. Do not call `Submission` or other Harness reads inside the callback:
	 * they wait for the commit holding the line. Its `pi.durable.submit` span covers the admission only, so its `result`
	 * is provisional. Throws for a transaction of another Session.
	 */
	admit(tx: Tx, submission: SubmissionDraft): Promise<SubmissionId>;
	/**
	 * Admit a write of a `pi.reset` entry that starts a new context, carrying `handoff` as a user message when given.
	 * Resolves after admission; while busy, it is placed at the next boundary.
	 */
	reset(handoff: string | undefined, context: Context): Promise<void>;
	/**
	 * Admit a manual compaction task and return its ID. It summarizes while the conversation keeps working and places its
	 * summary through a write submission: at once when idle, otherwise at the next boundary (spec §8.7).
	 */
	compact(instructions: string | undefined, context: Context): Promise<TaskId<CompactionResult>>;

	/** Session commit whose `tx.createTask()` defaults to this conversation; `options` as for `Session.commit()`. */
	commit<T>(change: (tx: Tx) => T | Promise<T>, context: Context, options?: CommitOptions): Promise<T>;
	/**
	 * Committed raw active transcript and model context. With `at`, the context as of that visible entry: the same view
	 * `fork(at)` would start with, without creating a conversation.
	 */
	context(context: Context, options?: { readonly at?: EntryId }): Promise<ContextView>;
	/** Fork-aware history of this conversation, newest first unless `query.order` is `ascending`. */
	entries(
		query: Omit<EntryQuery, "conversationId">,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<EntryRecord, Cursor>>;
	fork(at: EntryId, options: ConversationCreateOptions, context: Context): Promise<Conversation>;
	/**
	 * Withdraw queued inputs (queued writes stay), mark every live non-background task of the ordinary ownership scope,
	 * signal them, and resolve once the scope is idle. Background subtrees survive unless `background` is set.
	 */
	abort(context: Context, options?: ConversationAbortOptions): Promise<void>;
	/**
	 * Resolve when the ordinary ownership scope has no live non-background task: this conversation and the conversations
	 * owned, transitively, by its non-background tasks.
	 */
	waitForIdle(context: Context): Promise<void>;
	/**
	 * The structural view (spec §9.3) as a serialized watch; commits made while its listener runs arrive folded. Its
	 * `entries` are a window over the transcript, as `window` says: the newest 50 by default, then appends, dropping the
	 * oldest past 100. Built on the same mount as `Harness.observeConversation()`.
	 */
	watch(context: Context, window?: ConversationWindow): Promise<ConversationWatch>;
}

## ConversationAbortOptions  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Options of `Conversation.abort()`. */
export type ConversationAbortOptions = {
	/**
	 * Cross background boundaries: mark every live task reached ignoring the background flag when the abort is admitted,
	 * withdraw the queued inputs of every conversation reached, and wait until those tasks are terminal and the
	 * conversation is ordinarily idle. Background work created afterwards is neither marked nor awaited.
	 */
	readonly background?: boolean;
};

## ConversationCreateOptions  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
export type ConversationCreateOptions = {
	readonly ownership: ConversationOwnership;
	/** Applied in the creating commit after the creation hook's copy, before `init`. */
	readonly agent?: AgentChange;
	readonly init?: ConversationInit;
};

## ConversationHandle  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/**
 * Invocation-bound conversation operations for tasks and tools. Rejects after the invocation ends. `submit` and `admit`
 * take any submission, as `Conversation.submit()` and `Conversation.admit()`: a subagent's conversation is an ordinary
 * one, so a tool may also continue it, and a task may admit a submission in the same commit as its own writes
 * (`runtime.commit()`); entries the admission appends there carry the task's `byTaskId`. `admit` also rejects once the
 * invocation is aborted.
 */
export interface ConversationHandle {
	readonly id: ConversationId;
	submit(submission: SubmissionDraft, context: Context): Promise<Submission>;
	admit(tx: Tx, submission: SubmissionDraft): Promise<SubmissionId>;
	/** `Conversation.abort()`: withdraw queued inputs, abort the ordinary ownership scope, and wait until it is idle. */
	abort(context: Context, options?: ConversationAbortOptions): Promise<void>;
	/** Resolve when the conversation's ordinary ownership scope has no live non-background task. */
	waitForIdle(context: Context): Promise<void>;
}

## ConversationInit  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/**
 * Runs inside the creating commit, after the creation hook and the `agent` change. The conversation creation is already
 * a table write, so table reads here throw `ReadAfterWrite`; document access remains available.
 */
export type ConversationInit = (tx: Tx, conversationId: ConversationId) => void | Promise<void>;

	 * `codemode` section lists it while the extension is selected, also before it has any tools.

	readonly sections?: readonly PromptSection<Tool>[];

## GenerationHooks  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Hooks of the built-in generation task. */
export interface GenerationHooks {
	/** Before every request attempt, including recovery; the result is used for that request only. */
	beforeRequest(
		request: { readonly messages: readonly Message[] },
		api: HookApi,
		context: Context,
	): HookResult<{ readonly messages: readonly Message[] }>;
	/**
	 * After pi-ai builds the provider request body, before it is sent; the result replaces the body for that request only.
	 * Runs again whenever pi-ai rebuilds the body, such as a retry within one attempt. The body is in the provider API's
	 * own format (`request.model.api`), so a hook checks the API before changing it.
	 */
	beforeProviderRequest(
		request: { readonly model: Model<Api>; readonly payload: unknown },
		api: HookApi,
		context: Context,
	): HookResult<{ readonly payload: unknown }>;
	/** Every terminal provider message, before classification. */
	afterResponse(message: AssistantMessage, api: HookApi, context: Context): void | Promise<void>;
	/**
	 * A final answer; the first result wins. Kind `continue` appends a user message and continues the run. `tasks` decide
	 * whether the answer stands (spec suspendable §6): the answer is appended, the run's inputs stay open
	 * (`LiveRun.yield`), the tasks run as the generation's children, and the first in creation order that completes with
	 * a `YieldDecision` holding `continue` provides the continuation; without one the run ends with the answer.
	 */
	onYield(
		answer: AssistantMessage,
		api: HookApi,
		context: Context,
	): HookResult<
		| { readonly kind: "continue"; readonly continue: UserInput }
		| { readonly kind: "tasks"; readonly tasks: readonly HookTask[] }
	>;
	/**
	 * After every tool of the round is terminal; `results` are the round's result entries in call order. Requested tasks
	 * of every hook, concatenated in extension order, run as the generation's children before the round ends; one that
	 * completes with `{ terminate: true }` (`AfterToolsDecision`) ends the run as a round whose calls all asked to
	 * terminate. A task answers the run otherwise by submitting a steer in its terminal commit.
	 */
	afterTools(
		assistant: EntryId,
		results: readonly EntryId[],
		api: HookApi,
		context: Context,
	): HookResult<{ readonly tasks: readonly HookTask[] }>;
	/**
	 * After a run answered, its answer committed and its inputs settled `done`: a final answer, or a `terminate` round;
	 * not when an `onYield` continuation is taken, and never after a failure or an abort. The requested tasks of every
	 * hook are created together as children of the generation, which keeps the run, and the conversation busy, until
	 * they are terminal; then queued items are placed and the run ends (spec §8.3). A crash before they are created asks
	 * again; once created, never again for this run.
	 */
	afterRun(run: RunSummary, api: HookApi, context: Context): HookResult<{ readonly tasks: readonly HookTask[] }>;
}

## Harness  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect via Harness
/** Durable agent harness over one Session. */
export interface Harness extends Session {
	/**
	 * Enable task scheduling. Idempotent; throws after close, and `ReadOnlySession` on a read-only Harness. Calls that
	 * ask for progress enable it too: `Conversation.submit()`, `Conversation.compact()`, `Conversation.abort()`,
	 * `Submission.wait()`, `waitForTask()`, `Harness.waitForIdle()`, and `Conversation.waitForIdle()`. Read-only viewers
	 * never do.
	 */
	resume(): void;
	/**
	 * When this Session next needs a running process, from the scheduler's memory: `active` while some task can run now
	 * or is running, `at` for the earliest sleep. Answers also while scheduling is paused. A host that wakes the
	 * process itself, such as a Durable Object alarm, arms from it and calls `resume()` when woken; see
	 * `HarnessOptions.onWake`.
	 */
	wake(): Wake;

	/** Return the reserved root conversation, creating it with `agent` and `init` in one commit when absent. */
	root(
		context: Context,
		options?: { readonly agent?: AgentChange; readonly init?: ConversationInit },
	): Promise<Conversation>;
	conversation(id: ConversationId, context: Context): Promise<Conversation | undefined>;
	createConversation(options: ConversationCreateOptions, context: Context): Promise<Conversation>;

	getTask<R>(id: TaskId<R>, context: Context): Promise<TaskRecord<JsonValue, JsonValue, R> | undefined>;
	/** Live tasks and unsettled submissions. Writes nothing and runs no task code. */
	inspect(context: Context): Promise<HarnessInspection>;
	/** Reacquire a submission, for example after reopen. */
	submission(id: SubmissionId, context: Context): Promise<Submission | undefined>;
	/** `not_found` for an unknown submission or one of another conversation than `conversationId`. */
	abortSubmission(
		id: SubmissionId,
		context: Context,
		conversationId?: ConversationId,
	): Promise<"aborted" | "already_placed" | "settled" | "not_found">;
	/**
	 * Commit the abort mark, signal and join an active run invocation, and schedule the abort invocation. A task whose
	 * definition cannot take it settles as `orphaned` instead.
	 */
	abortTask(id: TaskId, context: Context): Promise<"marked" | "terminal">;
	/**
	 * `tx.signal()` in a commit of its own: deliver `value` to task `taskId` under `key`. Enables scheduling, so a host
	 * arms its recovery wakeup first, as before `submit()`. Checks nothing about the caller.
	 */
	signal<T>(taskId: TaskId, token: SignalToken<T>, key: string, value: T, context: Context): Promise<SignalResult>;
	/** Resolve with the terminal receipt; cancelling `context` cancels only this wait. */
	waitForTask<R>(id: TaskId<R>, context: Context): Promise<SettledTask<R>>;
	/** Resolve when the ordinary ownership scope of every ownerless conversation has no live non-background task. */
	waitForIdle(context: Context): Promise<void>;
	/** Session total: every conversation's `pi.usage` summed. */
	usage(context: Context): Promise<UsageState>;
	/**
	 * Every live task with its owner edge, status, and owned conversations (spec §9.4), as a serialized watch; commits
	 * made while its listener runs arrive folded.
	 */
	watchTaskGraph(context: Context): Promise<TaskGraphWatch>;
	/**
	 * Attach a synchronous `Observer` to a conversation's structural view (spec §9.3), atomically on the Session line,
	 * for adapters: `advance` gets each next revision with its operations as memory adopts the commit, inside Storage's
	 * `adopt` for a stored one and before it is stored for a deferred one, so it only records it. `window` as for
	 * `Conversation.watch()`; each observer has its own. `context` governs only the attachment.
	 */
	observeConversation(
		id: ConversationId,
		observer: Observer<ConversationView>,
		context: Context,
		window?: ConversationWindow,
	): Promise<Observation<ConversationView>>;
	/**
	 * Attach a synchronous `Observer` to the task graph (spec §9.4), as `observeConversation()` does to a view. A
	 * `blocked` reason that changes without a commit (a registry change, a failed migration) advances it on the Session
	 * line outside any commit and `adopt`, with the background context.
	 */
	observeTaskGraph(observer: Observer<TaskGraph>, context: Context): Promise<Observation<TaskGraph>>;
}

## HarnessInspection  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Point-in-time view of live work: unfinished tasks and submissions, read on the Session line. */
export type HarnessInspection = {
	readonly scheduling: "paused" | "running" | "closing";
	readonly tasks: readonly TaskInspection[];
	/** Queued and placed submissions, in ID order. */
	readonly submissions: readonly SubmissionRecord[];
};

## HarnessOptions  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
export type HarnessOptions<Tool extends ToolRegistration = ToolRegistration> = {
	/** Host-owned adapter for content-free admission/phase telemetry; propagation and metrics are optional. */
	readonly telemetry?: TelemetryContext;
	/**
	 * pi-ai model access used by generation, compaction, hooks and tools: a `Models`, or a function returning the current
	 * one, called at each use, so a host can replace its model configuration without reopening the Harness.
	 */
	readonly models: Models | (() => Models);
	/**
	 * How model requests identify the app to providers, merged field by field over `DEFAULT_HARNESS_IDENTITY`
	 * (`{ attribution: PI_ATTRIBUTION }`, provider attribution to pi). It applies to every request through the Harness's
	 * models, including hooks and tools, and overrides the identity the `Models` was created with; a request's own
	 * `identity` overrides it. Pass `{ attribution: null }` to send no attribution headers.
	 */
	readonly identity?: ClientIdentity;
	readonly registry: RegistryReader<Tool>;
	/** Run settings, or a function returning the current ones; read at each use either way. */
	readonly settings?: HarnessSettings | (() => HarnessSettings | undefined);
	/** Builds a conversation's environment at each use. Never called on the Session line; may be async. */
	readonly env?: (target: EnvTarget, context: Context) => ExecutionEnv | undefined | Promise<ExecutionEnv | undefined>;
	/**
	 * Runs in every commit that creates or forks a conversation, raw `tx.createConversation()` included, after the
	 * built-in `pi.*` documents and before the conveniences apply `agent` and run `init`. A fork already has its copies.
	 * Table reads throw `ReadAfterWrite`, as in `init`; a throw fails the creating commit.
	 */
	readonly conversationCreated?: (tx: Tx, conversation: ConversationRecord) => void | Promise<void>;
	/**
	 * The Harness clock, epoch milliseconds; default `Date.now`. Sleeping tasks store deadlines on it, so every process
	 * that opens the same storage must use the same clock.
	 */
	readonly now?: () => number;
	/**
	 * Arms the timers of the Session, the scheduler, and its tasks: pacing progress commits, freeing idle memory
	 * (`background`), and, without `onWake`, resuming sleeping tasks; and the timers of `TaskRuntime.setTimer()`. The
	 * Node.js environment, file watcher, and image worker keep their own timers. Default `setTimeout`, with background
	 * timers unreferenced, or declined in Cloudflare Workers and where they cannot be unreferenced. Tests can pass fake
	 * timers; a host can keep timers off a process that should hibernate.
	 */
	readonly setTimer?: SetTimer;
	/**
	 * Wakes the process for sleeping tasks instead of a `setTimer` timer. Without it, while scheduling runs, a timer that
	 * keeps the process alive resumes sleeping tasks when they are due. With it, the Harness arms no timer for them: it
	 * calls `onWake` after open and whenever `Harness.wake()` changes, and the host arms its own wakeup, such as a
	 * Durable Object alarm, and calls `resume()` when it fires. Called in a microtask the Session line never waits for,
	 * after the commit that changed the value was adopted, so a host arms a recovery wakeup before calls that can start
	 * work. It may call `wake()` and `resume()`, and must not block. A throw is reported, and the value is offered again
	 * at the next change.
	 */
	readonly onWake?: (wake: Wake) => void;
	/**
	 * Receives failures that do not fail the calling operation, such as a throwing hook or listener, a task that faulted,
	 * and the error that fails the Session, once: one `Report`, the `error` and what happened (`kind` and the fields of
	 * its `ReportInfo`). A host can tell a failed Session (`storage_failed`, often a platform reset) from a faulted task
	 * (`task_faulted`). Its own throw or rejection is dropped.
	 */
	readonly onReport?: (report: Report) => void;
	/**
	 * Open for reading only, as a viewer of a session that another process drives, for example a synced copy on a device
	 * that only shows it. Open recovers nothing: a `running` task stays as committed. Every commit with writes rejects
	 * with `ReadOnlySession` before it reaches Storage, and so does `resume()` and every call that enables scheduling;
	 * the Harness stays usable for reads and watches. `wake()` is always inactive, and `onWake` is never called. Reopen
	 * without it to write.
	 */
	readonly readOnly?: boolean;
};

## HarnessSettings  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Harness-wide run policy. Read at every resolution and never copied; getters are fine. Synchronous: some readers run on the Session line. */
export type HarnessSettings = {
	/** Default extension selection; absent: every installed extension, in install order. */
	readonly extensions?: readonly Extension[];
	readonly stream?: ConversationStreamOptions;
	readonly retry?: Partial<ConversationRetryPolicy>;
	readonly compaction?: CompactionSettings;
	readonly progress?: Partial<ProgressPolicy>;
	readonly toolExecution?: ToolExecutionMode;
	readonly steeringMode?: QueueMode;
	readonly followUpMode?: QueueMode;
	/**
	 * How long an inactive conversation keeps its last context read in memory, so its next run reads only newer entries.
	 * Inactive: idle, or with all its live work parked (sleeping, waiting, or holding an outcome). Active conversations
	 * always keep it; `0` drops it once the conversation is inactive.
	 */
	readonly contextRetentionMs?: number;
	/**
	 * How long a loaded document that no watch observes stays in memory after its last read or write;
	 * the next access loads it from Storage. Observed documents always stay. Default ten minutes; `0` drops one right
	 * after use; `Infinity` keeps them. Anything else that is not a number of milliseconds means the default.
	 */
	readonly documentRetentionMs?: number;
	/**
	 * What a run that fails (`model_error`, `no_model`, `interrupted`, `restart_limit`, `nothing_to_answer`,
	 * `turn_limit`) does with the inputs queued behind it: `keep` leaves them queued until the next input or queued write, `continue` starts the
	 * next run with them, as an answer would, and `withdraw` settles them `unanswered` with reason `run_failed`. Default
	 * `keep`.
	 */
	readonly afterFailedRun?: AfterFailedRun;
	/**
	 * How many times in a row a task may be cut off by a crash, eviction, or reset (a close does not count) without
	 * changing its state before it ends instead of running again: a tool call with an error result, a compaction failed
	 * into `pi.live.compactionFailure`, a run with `pi.live.runFailure` reason `restart_limit`, any other task `faulted`
	 * with detail `{ reason: "restart_limit" }`. A generation's request or poll the host died during is a failed attempt
	 * under `retry` first; the limit bounds it only when charging that attempt keeps being cut off. Default 5;
	 * `Infinity` never ends a task for it.
	 */
	readonly restartLimit?: number;
};

## HookApi  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/**
 * What a hook may use: committed reads and the asking task's memos, which hooks and the task share. Hooks run off the
 * Session line, so reads see what is committed when they run; a hook rerun after a crash may see more.
 */
export interface HookApi extends DocumentReader {
	readonly taskId: TaskId;
	readonly conversationId: ConversationId;
	/** The current `HarnessOptions.models`, read at each access. */
	readonly models: Models;
	memo<T extends JsonValue>(name: string, context: Context): Promise<T | undefined>;
	memo<T extends JsonValue>(name: string, candidate: T, context: Context): Promise<T>;
	/** A signal key's committed state in the asking task, as `TaskRuntime.readSignal()`. */
	readSignal<T>(token: SignalToken<T>, key: string, context: Context): Promise<SignalState<T> | undefined>;
	/** The Harness clock. */
	now(): number;
	/** Committed entry visible from the task's conversation, as `TaskRuntime.entry()`. */
	entry(id: EntryId, context: Context): Promise<EntryRecord | undefined>;
	/** Undefined when the entry is absent, not visible, or has another kind. */
	entry<D extends JsonValue>(token: Entry<D>, id: EntryId, context: Context): Promise<TypedEntry<D> | undefined>;
	/** Committed raw history of the task's conversation, as `TaskRuntime.entries()`. */
	entries(
		query: Omit<EntryQuery, "conversationId">,
		limit: number,
		cursor: Cursor | undefined,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<Page<EntryRecord, Cursor>>;
}

## NestedToolExecutionResult  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/**
 * Result of a nested call, as `executeTool()` returns it. Programs read `structuredOutput`; the output for the model
 * is not kept, and `control` does not apply.
 */
export type NestedToolExecutionResult = {
	/** The nested call's tool task. */
	readonly taskId: TaskId;
	/**
	 * The tool's value for programs. A tool with `structuredOutputSchema`: its validated `structuredOutput`, also on an
	 * error result that has one; absent otherwise, and an error's text is then in an error diagnostic. A tool without:
	 * its bounded output, success or error, as a string for one text item, an `ImageContent` for one image, `""` for
	 * none, and the content list otherwise. Absent on an error result the Harness wrote itself (unavailable, invalid,
	 * blocked, interrupted, aborted); `diagnostics` say what went wrong.
	 */
	readonly structuredOutput?: JsonValue;
	readonly isError: boolean;
	readonly details?: JsonValue;
	readonly diagnostics: readonly ToolDiagnostic[];
	readonly usage?: Usage;
	/** Execution time of the attempt that produced the result; absent when it never executed. */
	readonly durationMs?: number;
};

## NoResultFields  durable/src/harness/types.ts

## ProgressPolicy  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/**
 * How often running progress is committed, and how long it may wait in memory before it is stored. Progress commits are
 * deferred (`CommitPersistence`): watches see each at once, and Storage gets them together, at the run's next phase
 * boundary or after `persistWithinMs`. A host can commit less often, so live answers and tool output appear in larger steps.
 */
export type ProgressPolicy = {
	/** Minimum pause between commits of the answer being generated. */
	partialIntervalMs: number;
	/** Minimum pause between commits of running tool output; large commits also pause in proportion to their size. */
	outputIntervalMs: number;
	/**
	 * How long these commits, and other deferred commits without their own `withinMs`, may stay in memory before they are
	 * stored (`CommitPersistence`); a crash loses at most about this much of an answer or of tool output. Default 1,000;
	 * `Infinity` stores them only at the next commit that reads or writes their document and at close.
	 */
	persistWithinMs: number;
};

	readonly agent: Agent<Tool>;
	/** Built by `HarnessOptions.env` for this preparation; `undefined` without an environment. */
	readonly env: ExecutionEnv | undefined;
	/** Sections already in effect after replaying the active transcript. */
	readonly shown: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
	/** Committed document reads. */
	readonly read: DocumentReader;
};

## Registry  durable/src/harness/types.ts

## RegistryReader  durable/src/harness/types.ts

/** Read side of a registry consumed by a Harness. */
export interface RegistryReader<Tool extends ToolRegistration = ToolRegistration> {
	/** Immutable view of the whole current registry. */
	snapshot(): RegistrySnapshot<Tool>;
	/** Called synchronously after every publication; wakes the scheduler to reconsider blocked tasks. */
	subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void;
}

## RegistrySnapshot  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Immutable view of one published registry state. */
export interface RegistrySnapshot<Tool extends ToolRegistration = ToolRegistration> {
	installed(): readonly Extension<Tool>[];

	/** Every installed tool with its extension, in install order. Names may repeat across extensions. */
	tools(): readonly { readonly extension: Extension<Tool>; readonly tool: Tool }[];
	sections(): readonly { readonly extension: Extension<Tool>; readonly section: PromptSection<Tool> }[];
	/** Built-in and installed task definitions. */
	tasks(): readonly AnyTask[];
	task(name: string): AnyTask | undefined;
}

	 * The run's first entry (`LiveRun.first`): the first one the boundary that started it placed, for a continue the failed

	readonly answer: EntryId;

## Submission  durable/src/harness/types.ts

export interface Submission {

## SubmissionDraft  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/**
 * Host submission: user input that may start a run, a passive entry write, or a continue: a run without a new user
 * message, for an idle conversation whose context the model still owes an answer (it ends in a user message or tool
 * results, for example after a run that ended without an answer).
 */
export type SubmissionDraft = {
	readonly requestId?: string;
	/**
	 * When the submission settles, deliver `SubmissionSettled` (the settled record) to `notify.taskId` under
	 * `notify.key`, in the settling commit; a delivery the task refuses (`closed`, `not_found`) fails nothing. A
	 * submission that settles before the task sleeps on the key wakes the sleep at once.
	 */
	readonly notify?: SubmissionNotify;
} & (
	| {
			readonly type: "input";
			readonly content: UserInput;
			readonly whenBusy?: "steer" | "followUp" | "reject";
			/**
			 * `reject`: an idle conversation (no run) rejects the input with `ConversationIdle` and writes nothing, so the input
			 * never starts a run of its own. With `whenBusy: "steer"` it steers the current run or is refused; a run that
			 * answered and waits for its `afterRun` tasks is still busy, and such an input queues and starts the next run.
			 */
			readonly whenIdle?: "reject";
			/**
			 * What `Conversation.abort()` and abort cascades do with the input while it is queued: `withdraw` (default)
			 * settles it `unanswered` with reason `aborted`; `keep` leaves it queued, as a failed run leaves its queue under
			 * `afterFailedRun: "keep"`, so the next input places it and that run answers it. For input its sender cannot
			 * take back, such as another agent's message. `Submission.abort()` withdraws it either way.
			 */
			readonly onAbort?: "withdraw" | "keep";
			/** Place the input as this entry; default `pi.user` without data. The kind must not start with `pi.`. */
			readonly entry?: InputEntry;
	  }
	| {
			readonly type: "write";
			readonly entry: EntryDraft;
			readonly content?: never;
			readonly whenBusy?: never;
			readonly whenIdle?: never;
	  }
	| {
			/**
			 * Start a run on the context as it is, without a user message. Only when idle: a busy conversation rejects it with
			 * `ConversationBusy`, and it never queues. Items kept in `pi.inbox` are placed first and join the run. A context
			 * with nothing to answer (empty, or ending in an answer, also a text answer cut off at its output limit) ends the
			 * run without a request, `unanswered` with `nothing_to_answer`. A cut-off answer with tool calls is continued:
			 * its calls never ran, and the context ends in their error results (`missing_result`).
			 */
			readonly type: "continue";
			readonly content?: never;
			readonly entry?: never;
			readonly whenBusy?: never;
			readonly whenIdle?: never;
	  }
);

## TaskInspection  durable/src/harness/types.ts
used by: durable-effect
/** Live task and what the scheduler would do with it under the current registry. */
export type TaskInspection = {
	readonly record: TaskRecord<JsonValue, JsonValue, JsonValue>;
	readonly state: /** An invocation is active. */
		| { readonly kind: "running" }
		/** The next scheduling pass reserves it; `migrates` when its definition is newer and has `migrate`. */
		| { readonly kind: "pending"; readonly migrates: boolean }
		/**
		 * Waits for these live tasks: the live part of its `on`, or, when abort-marked, its live ordinary owned work, which
		 * must end before its abort handler starts.
		 */
		| { readonly kind: "waiting"; readonly on: readonly TaskId[] }
		/** Sleeps until the Harness clock reaches `until`, if set, or a signal it sleeps on arrives. */
		| { readonly kind: "sleeping"; readonly until?: number }
		/** Outcome held until its ordinary owned work drains. */
		| { readonly kind: "completing" }
		/** Cannot run here: no registered definition can take it (aborting it settles it as `orphaned`). */
		| {
				readonly kind: "blocked";
				readonly reason: "missing_task" | "task_too_old" | "migration_failed";
				readonly error?: unknown;
		  };
};
